attributes.body:
と言（い）ってもいい is a common expression in Japanese which literally means 'even if you say (A), it is good/ok'. This is translated more naturally as 'you could say (A)', or 'you might say (A)'.

As the と at the beginning of the phrase is the 'quotation' use of the と particle, と言（い）ってもいい may be used after almost any statement that the speaker wants to quote.

Fun Fact

Most grammatical structures in Japanese that use 言（い）う will often appear without kanji. This is simply to make them easier to recognize as a grammar pattern, rather than a standard word in a sentence. This is also true for patterns that include 行（い）く, or 来（く）る.

attributes.description: Learn と言ってもいい in Japanese!

attributes.body: と is a quoting particle used to mark the content of direct or indirect speech, thoughts, or feelings. For example, 行くと言っていた means '[He] was saying [he] will go.' といってもいい combines と with 言う and the い-Adjective いい, meaning 'You/one could say' (literally, 'It's fine even if one says...').

first_relatable.title: といってもいい
first_relatable.meaning: You could say, You might say

attributes.body: Both と言える and といってもいい can express a meaning similar to the English 'it can/might be said that (A)' with the difference being the degree of assertiveness. と言える is a firmer statement, literally meaning '(A) can be said.'. In contrast, といってもいい sounds more tentative, implying that it would be fine/acceptable to say the thing in question, but allowing for the possibility that other views/opinions may also be valid.

attributes.body: The ても form has the core meaning of 'even if.' One common use is Verb + てもいい, which gives or asks for permission—for example, 食べてもいいですか？ literally means 'Is it okay even if I eat this?' but works like 'Can/May I eat this?' in English. Similarly, といってもいい means 'It's okay even if you say...' but is used to express 'You could say' or 'One might say.'

second_relatable.title: Verb + てもいい
second_relatable.meaning: It's okay to, It's alright to, Can/may

attributes.body: These forms are similar in that both can make a statement sound less certain, but their nuance differs. ないでもない uses a double negative, literally 'It's not not (A).', to express a somewhat unsure positive, e.g., 分からないでもない ('I kind of understand.', or literally 'It's not that I don't understand.'). といってもいい suggests 'you could say (A)', e.g. 問題ないといってもいい ('You could say there's no problem.').

attributes.body: って (a contracted form of と) is a casual quoting particle used to mark direct or indirect speech, thoughts, feelings, or to introduce a topic casually. For example, 行くって言っていた means '[They] were saying [they] will go.' といってもいい combines と with 言う and いい, meaning 'You/one could say' (literally: 'It's fine even if one says...').
